newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SFE wheat drifts as options attract the trade.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SFE wheat drifts as options attract the trade.

text.p: Wheat futures option trades again outnumbered futures trades on the Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) on Tuesday as brokers said the market appeared likely to continue to drift down.
Five futures lots traded in the January contract, which surprised by rising A$1.50 on the sale to A$170.00 a tonne.
Settlement quotes on wheat futures were generally down by about A$1.00 on the close.
Twenty put options also traded in the A$170 January contract at a A$9.00 premium.
Kerrin Gleeson of Elders Risk Management Pty Ltd said selling pressure still dominated the market. Not many were keen to buy at present levels, she said.
"I can't see the market heading anywhere else (but down) with Chicago coming off and all the bearish reports around. There really seems only way for it to go at the moment," she said.
In the cash market, the Australian Wheat Board's indicative quotes for new crop wheat and sorghum were cut by A$3.00 a tonne.
